hello.note: Polite, for anyone during the day. Friends say Привіт (prih-VEET), hi

how-are-you.note: More formal: Як ваші справи? (yak VA-shee SPRA-vih)

im-well.note: The same for a man or a woman

good-night.note: Only when parting at night. Good evening is Добрий вечір (DOB-rihy VE-cheer)

please.note: Also means you're welcome and here you are

thank-you.note: Щиро дякую (SHCHIH-ro DYA-koo-yoo) means thank you very much

youre-welcome.note: Also: Нема за що (ne-MA za shcho), it's nothing

no.note: Ні, дякую (nee, DYA-koo-yoo) is no, thank you

excuse-me.note: Sorry, and excuse me to get attention or get past

my-name.note: Literally "they call me", the same for a man or a woman. The audio uses Peter as the example name

your-name.note: Polite, with вас (vas), the respectful you

where-from.note: Answer Я з... (ya z), I'm from...

dont-understand.note: The same for a man or a woman

thousand.note: Prices are in hryvnias (HRIHV-nya), written ₴ or грн

how-much.note: Point and say Скільки це коштує? (tse), how much is this?

would-like.note: The polite way to order. A woman says хотіла. The audio uses каву (KA-voo), a coffee, as the example

i-want.note: More direct. Add будь ласка. The audio uses оце (o-TSE), this one, as the example

do-you-have.note: Literally "is there ... at yours?" The audio uses вода (vo-DA), water, as the example

just-looking.note: The same for a man or a woman

discount.note: Bargaining is only for markets. Можна (MOZH-na), may I?, starts any polite request

card.note: Literally "may I pay by card?" Cards and phone payments work almost everywhere

bill.note: A tip of about 10% is usual in restaurants

checkout-time.note: Literally "at what time is moving out?"

toilet.note: Де (de) means where. Ж is for women, Ч for men

taxi.note: Apps like Uklon and Bolt are widely used

train.note: Ukraine's trains, run by Ukrzaliznytsia, are the main way to travel long distances

bus.note: A shared minibus is a маршрутка (mar-SHROOT-ka)

which-train.note: After до (do), to, the place changes its ending: Львів (lveew), Lviv, becomes Львова (LVO-va). The audio uses Lviv as the example

buy-ticket.note: Train tickets are also sold in the Ukrzaliznytsia app

two-tickets.note: The audio uses Lviv as the example
two-tickets.spoken: Два квитки до Львова, будь ласка

trip-length.note: Literally "how much to travel to...?" The audio uses Lviv

allergic.note: Literally "I have an allergy to", the same for a man or a woman. Add the food: горіхи (ho-REE-khih) nuts, арахіс (a-RA-khees) peanuts, рибу (RIH-boo) fish. The audio uses nuts

love-dish.note: Literally "this dish tastes very good to me", the same for anyone

what-called.note: Point at the dish or item

table-for-two.note: For more people: на трьох (tryokh), 3, or на чотирьох (cho-tih-RYOKH), 4

coffee.note: Lviv is famous for its coffee houses

water.note: Still is без газу (bez HA-zoo), sparkling з газом (z HA-zom)

hot.note: Hot, of food and drinks. Hot weather is спекотно (spe-KOT-no). Spicy is гостре (HOS-tre)

cold.note: Cold, of food and drinks. Cold weather is холодно (KHO-lod-no)

cheers.note: Literally "let us be!" The answer is Гей! (hey)

help.note: Shout it. For any emergency call 112; police are on 102

need-doctor.note: The same for a man or a woman. For an ambulance, call 103 or 112

pharmacy.note: Look for the green cross; many are open 24 hours
